questions.enonce_markdown:
State FOUR features of any TWO of the following:

(i) Supermarkets,

(ii) Department stores,

(iii) Hyper markets, and

(iv) Multiple shops.

(8 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** The question asks for any TWO types of large-scale retail shop, with four features each (2 x 4 = 8 marks). The four types are given here so that the learner can revise all of them; a candidate answers only two.

**(i) Supermarkets**

1. A large retail shop that sells mainly food and household goods under one roof.
2. It works on **self-service**: customers take a basket or trolley, pick the goods from shelves and pay at a checkout counter.
3. Goods are pre-packed, priced and clearly displayed.
4. It buys in bulk and has few sales staff, so it can sell at low prices; it is usually in a town centre or a residential area, often with a car park.

**(ii) Department stores**

1. A very large shop divided into departments, each selling a different class of goods (clothing, shoes, furniture, electrical goods, and so on), all under one roof.
2. Each department is placed under a departmental manager, but the whole store is controlled by a central management.
3. It offers extra services such as home delivery, credit, a restaurant, a car park and after-sales service.
4. It is usually in the centre of a big town, where there are many customers, and it offers a wide choice, so customers get "one-stop shopping".

**(iii) Hypermarkets**

1. A very big self-service store, larger than a supermarket, with a huge floor area.
2. It sells food and non-food goods (clothes, electrical goods, furniture) at the same place.
3. It is usually built on the edge of a town with a very large car park, so that customers can reach it by car.
4. It buys in very large quantities and sells at low prices, which attracts many customers.

**(iv) Multiple shops (chain stores)**

1. A chain of retail shops with many branches in different towns, all owned by one company.
2. Every branch sells the same range of goods, usually of one kind (shoes, clothing, pharmacy), with the same name, shop front and prices.
3. Buying is done centrally in very large quantities, which gives big trade discounts; each branch has a manager who follows the head office rules.
4. Branches are placed in busy shopping streets where many customers pass.

(Any TWO types with FOUR features each earn the 8 marks.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
Outline FOUR reasons for the continuous existence of small shops.

(8 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** Although large shops exist, small shops (kiosks, boutiques, neighbourhood shops and market stalls) remain very numerous. The reasons are as follows.

1. **Convenient location.** Small shops are near the homes of consumers, so people buy there at once without travelling to a distant town.

2. **Personal service and friendly relations.** The owner knows the customers and their tastes, greets them and gives advice. Customers feel at ease and become loyal.

3. **Credit to regular customers.** The shopkeeper can allow a trusted neighbour to buy now and pay later, which large self-service shops rarely do.

4. **Selling in small quantities (breaking bulk).** People with small incomes can buy a cup of rice or a single sachet of tomato paste instead of a large pack, which large shops do not offer.

5. **Long and flexible opening hours.** Many small shops open early and close late, and the owner may open on request.

6. **Low start-up and running cost.** A small shop needs little capital, and the owner and family often work without paid staff, so some prices can be kept low.

7. **Goods that large shops do not sell.** Some small shops specialise in a special product or sell goods for a particular group.

(Any FOUR reasons, each outlined, earn 4 x 2 = 8 marks.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
Briefly explain the following terms:

(i) Impulse buying

(ii) Self service.

(4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Impulse buying** is the purchase of goods **on the spur of the moment, without having planned it before entering the shop**. It is caused by attractive displays, packaging, special offers or goods placed near the checkout. For example, a customer who goes to buy bread and leaves with biscuits and a drink because they were well displayed.

**(ii) Self-service** is a method of retailing in which **customers choose the goods themselves** from shelves or racks, put them in a basket or trolley and **pay at a checkout** counter, without the help of a salesman. Goods are pre-packed and priced. It is used in supermarkets and hypermarkets and it saves labour cost.

(2 marks for each term.)
